text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'argentum-prod' GPU saturation detected (98% avg) — queue growing. Paging on-call @jason.lee :rotating_light:

jason.lee: Oncall Jason here. Looking at metrics now.

anna.martin: I'm checking autoscaler and burst config for argentum-prod. Seen any recent deploys?

jason.lee: No deploys in last 2h. Prom metrics show sustained tokens/s spike from tenant Argentum.

tom.kim: Repro'ing GPU queue. Running ssh to pool manager and dumping queue.

tom.kim: ```
POOL: argentum-prod
GPU_UTIL: 98
QUEUE_LEN: 312
RUNNING_JOBS: 46
WAITING_JOBS: 266
TOP_CONSUMER: tenant=argentum job=embeddings-batch-92 user=svc-embed
```

sara.rodriguez: Support: Argentum account manager (paul) is on call too, looping them in. Customer impact?

paul.mccoy: Paul (AM) — I've got Argentum on the line, they report timeouts for some internal endpoints (latency 5-12s) but no full outages. They're seeing degraded throughput.

nancy.cooper: CS: They've pushed a large embeddings sweep this morning, possibly scheduled. Asking them to pause if possible.

anna.martin: Autoscaler logs show no new GPU nodes added — burst was disabled for this pool (policy: manual approval required).

jason.lee: Options: 1) Approve manual burst to add 4 GPUs from spare capacity, 2) Evict non-critical jobs in pool, 3) Force-fallback to smaller model for Argentum (requires product/ops coordination). Thoughts?

tom.kim: Eviction candidates: maintenance-backfill jobs (labels: noninteractive=true) ~18 jobs freeing ~6 GPUs. Can start eviction now.

anna.martin: Approve immediate eviction of noninteractive jobs, then open burst if queue still >100 after 5m.

paul.mccoy: I'll ask Argentum to throttle their sweep for 10m. They agreed to pause new sweeps for now.

nancy.cooper: Notifying Argentum contact: "we're mitigating — pausing bulk work helps; we'll update in 10m" :white_check_mark:

jason.lee: Initiating eviction plan. @tom.kim run eviction controller with dry-run=false.

tom.kim: ```bash
# evict noninteractive batch jobs in argentum-prod
kubectl --context=pool-mgr -n argentum-prod label selector "noninteractive=true" | xargs kubectl delete pod --grace-period=30
```

tom.kim: Evictions started. Monitoring GPU util...

incident-bot: EVENT: evictions started (initiated by tom.kim) — tracking.

jason.lee: 90s in: GPU_UTIL -> 85, QUEUE_LEN -> 188. Good drop but still high.

anna.martin: Queue trending down. If queue remains >150 after 5m we should enable burst. I can approve burst now — provisioning 3 GPUs from spare pool.

paul.mccoy: Argentum confirmed pause, appreciative. They want ETA on recovery.

jason.lee: Approve burst. anna, please trigger. I'll coordinate fallback plan if needed.

anna.martin: Triggering manual burst: `redwoodctl pools burst argentum-prod --count 3 --reason "emergency capacity"`

incident-bot: ACTION: burst requested by anna.martin. Provisioning started.

anna.martin: Provisioning complete. New GPUs live. Monitoring.

anna.martin: GPU_UTIL -> 65, QUEUE_LEN -> 72. Latency improving.

paul.mccoy: Sharing status with customer: "We've added capacity and evicted non-critical work; you should see normal throughput returning. We'll monitor and follow up with a post-incident note."

nancy.cooper: CS to schedule follow-up call and advise on rate limits for future sweeps.

jason.lee: Post-incident actions: 1) Evaluate auto-burst policy for argentum-prod (policy currently manual) 2) Run cost estimate for recurring burst 3) Add detection rule for large scheduled batch sweeps. Assign owners?

anna.martin: I'll own (1) and (2).

nancy.cooper: I'll own (3) and CS outreach.

tom.kim: I'll collect eviction logs and pod list for postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: argentum-prod GPU saturation mitigated — status: recovered (monitoring). Paging cleared.

jason.lee: Thanks team. Filing incident brief and linking to this thread. :thumbsup:
